articles.title: Champions Cup: Connacht 45-36 Saracens - Hosts score seven tries in pool victory
articles.summary: Connacht produce a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.
articles.body:
Tries: Prendergast 2, Forde, Hurley-Langton, Frawley 2, Blade Cons: Gilbert 5

Tries: Vaenuku 2, Caluori, Tompkins, Segun, Daly Cons: Farrell 3

Connacht produced a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.

Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley scored two tries apiece as Connacht, third from bottom in the United Rugby Championship table after three games, crossed seven times against the three-time Champions Cup winners at a raucous Dexcom Stadium.

Saracens had the chance to leave with a losing bonus point, but Owen Farrell's conversion attempt after Elliot Daly's late try went wide.

The Prem club had led 12-0 early on with tries from Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori.

However, Connacht replied with 19 unanswered points as Prendergast, Cathal Forde and Shamus Hurley-Langton all touched down to put the hosts in front.

Hurley-Langton was sin-binned just before the break and Saracens took advantage almost immediately as Nick Tompkins dummied his way over the line from close range with the clock in the red, meaning an enthralling first half ended 19-19.

Connacht, still with 14 men, scored first in the second period when Bundee Aki set up Prendergast's second, although Saracens' response was swift as Farrell and Daly provided an easy run-in for Rotimi Segun.

Frawley's double and another from replacement Caolin Blade helped Connacht build a 14-point gap, despite centre Vaenuku scoring his second for the visitors, which proved more than enough to see out a hugely impressive victory.

A bonus point eluded Connacht, however, with teams needing to score three or more tries than their opponents to earn one in the pool stage this season.

Elsewhere in Pool Two on Saturday, La Rochelle beat South African side Lions 31-14.

Lions played the match in honour of team-mate Hyron Andrews , who died at the team's hotel on Friday aged 31, with tributes paid to the former Sale Sharks player before kick-off.

articles.title: Hyron Andrews: Lions and Sale Sharks among clubs to pay tribute to late South African lock
articles.summary: Lions and Sale Sharks are among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.
articles.body:
Lions and Sale Sharks were among the clubs to pay tribute to Hyron Andrews at their matches on Saturday, following the South African's death aged 31.

Former Sale lock Andrews died at the Lions' team hotel on Friday, a day before their Champions Cup pool game against La Rochelle in France.

The Lions, who said they would fulfil the fixture in Andrews' honour, lost 31-14.

Asked before the match why the Lions had chosen to play, head coach Ivan van Rooyen said: "It's been a tough 24 hours and we've decided to celebrate Hyron, show respect to his wife and his children, and celebrate life. It gets taken away so quickly.

"We've had hundreds and thousands of messages from all over the world.

"It's not about winning or losing today. It's not about rugby.

"We want to show the respect to Hyron, who was an unbelievable guy, an unbelievable player, a world-class dad and a world-class husband.

"Us arriving for the game shows how much he means to us and how much it means to everyone."

There was prolonged applause from La Rochelle supporters as the Lions players entered the field, and also after the minute's silence that was observed before kick-off.

Both sides wore black armbands and several players shed tears during the period of silence, while Andrews' number five jersey was laid out on the turf in front of the Lions' team.

Three South African players in La Rochelle's squad - Dillyn Leyds, David Kriel and Salmaan Moerat - then presented a commemorative jersey to their opponents.

There were pre-match tributes before all of this weekend's Champions Cup and Challenge Cup fixtures, including at Andrews' former club Sale.

Andrews spent just over two years with the Prem club before departing at the end of last season and returning to his native South Africa.

Speaking after their 47-27 loss to Glasgow Warriors, Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I am really impressed with how the lads have come together, looked after each other and got tighter in the trauma of it.

"It is a good indication of the strength of the squad and the depth of the culture, how much they want to get around each other and get through it together.

"Hyron represents a large portion of the squad, in that he came here under-rated and got opportunities to show what he is capable of.

"He forwarded his career, made Manchester his second home, settled with his wife and had another child.

"He left with a lot of good mates and people who consider him as one of their best mates. His impact and what he gave off the field was far more from what he gave on it. It is still really raw to process.

"His two boys are too young to really fathom what is going on but I know the lads close to Hyron have been speaking to his two boys already this morning.

"We will help their family get through it."

articles.title: Champions Cup: Bath 14-32 Montpellier - French side excel in second half to win
articles.summary: Montpellier score 22 second-half points without reply to beat Bath on the opening weekend of the Champions Cup.
articles.body:
Tries: Hogg, Taofifenua 2, Becognee Cons: Hastings 3 Pens: Hastings 2

Montpellier earned an impressive victory at Bath, rounding off a disappointing Saturday for English clubs in the Champions Cup.

After Gloucester's high-scoring draw against holders Bordeaux on Friday, Bath joined Sale, Bristol and Saracens in losing their opening pool fixture.

Leicester, Exeter and Northampton are all in action on Sunday.

Bath had scored at least 33 points in each of their first three Prem games this season but failed to reach those heights in attack during their Pool Four opener at The Rec.

The hosts had a try disallowed in both halves, while Joe Cokanasiga failed to cleanly gather a pass with the tryline beckoning when they led 14-10 early in the second period.

Bath were punished by Donovan Taofifenua's second-half double and an Alex Becognee try for last season's Challenge Cup winners Montpellier, who scored 22 points without reply after half-time.

Recap: Saturday's Champions Cup action as it happened

Bath had already had a Max Ojomoh try ruled out for a knock-on when Montpellier's former Scotland full-back Stuart Hogg raced in for the first points of the match.

The hosts would soon be on the scoreboard themselves as England centre Ollie Lawrence barged over in the corner, before number eight Arthur Green brilliantly sidestepped past a defender to put the Prem club in front.

Montpellier, beaten Top 14 finalists last season, kept in touch with an Adam Hastings penalty before the interval.

Cokanasiga's missed opportunity proved costly almost immediately as winger Taofifenua dived over in the corner to make it 15-14 in the French side's favour.

Hastings added a further three points from the tee and after an excellent defensive spell by the visitors, Taofifenua intercepted a Finn Russell pass on halfway and sped away from the chasing Bath defenders to score his second.

Josh Bayliss' try for Bath did not stand because of an infringement earlier in the move, and Becognee burrowed over from close range in the final few minutes for Montpellier to make the win safe.

Bath's remaining pool fixtures are against Cardiff, South African side Bulls and Stade Francais.

The latter two of those teams met earlier on Saturday, with Bulls scoring eight tries in a convincing 56-20 victory against their French opponents.

Cheswill Jooste ended with a hat-trick, having opened the scoring inside 20 seconds, in a bonus-point win.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: New Zealand avoid massive shock against Fiji
articles.summary: New Zealand women are given a World Cup "wake-up call" after they are forced to come from behind to beat debutants Fiji in their opening game.
articles.body:
New Zealand women were given a World Cup "wake-up call" after they were forced to come from behind to beat debutants Fiji in their opening game.

The Ferns are one of the most successful teams in women's rugby league history – they have reached the final of all six World Cups, winning the first three before finishing runners up to Australia in the previous three years.

They are generally considered second favourites this time around and were expected to win easily against the Fijians in Newcastle on Sunday.

Instead, New Zealand were made to battle to an 18-12 win, having trailed 12-4 in the first half.

They were 12-10 down at the break – the first time they have ever been behind at half-time in a World Cup match.

"I've not really got any nails left. Or teeth," New Zealand coach Ricky Henry told his post-match news conference.

McDermott seeks fix as England fight to save their World Cup

England crush Women's World Cup debutants Wales

Brown scores stunner as England thrash World Cup debutants Wales

"The good thing is we found a way, but the way we played is not what we should.

"We went away from what we were meant to do, so we are a little disappointed there. Rustiness is not an excuse.

"I reckon it's a wake-up call, and the girls will think so too. We fought our way back, so we will take that away with things to work on."

New Zealand looked to be on course for a comfortable day when Stacey Waaka scored after two minutes, but Fiji grew into the match before scoring after 21 minutes.

Skipper Sereana Naitokatoka made a clever run from dummy half to find Losana Lutu who scored Fiji's first women's World Cup try

And when Sienna Laing extended the lead five minutes later, suddenly the upset looked on.

Waaka scored her second try to close the gap before the break, but after the interval Fiji's staunch defence still refused to give way.

But the pressure eventually told as New Zealand levelled then took the lead from Zehara Temara penalty kicks.

The win was not secured until the final minutes when Raecene McGregor's cross-field kick found Leianne Tufuga to score.

"We didn't put any expectations on ourselves, but they played like they had nothing to lose," New Zealand player Georgia Hale said. "They tested our waters for sure.

"Everything was in our control, then we lost it. It was uncharacteristically ill-disciplined, untidy play.

"What we wanted to do today was basic. We wanted to set the tone for the tournament by being physical and by going forwards, but we went far away from that which is not us.

"We then had to work extremely hard to make up for it. It was definitely luck in the end."

New Zealand face France at home in Christchurch next in Group B, while Fiji play Papua New Guinea.

Fiji aim to disrupt 'two-horse race' in men's World Cup

In the men's World Cup, Fiji made a strong start to their competition with a 40-12 win over Cook Islands in Newcastle.

The two sides are in Group A, alongside co-hosts Australia and New Zealand, so face a tough ask to finish in the top two and reach the semi-finals.

Fiji have endured a turbulent build-up, with Mick Potter replacing Wise Kativerata as head coach, a power struggle within the national governing body, and captain Tui Kamikamica having to retire after suffering a stroke in March.

But they gave themselves a boost with a comfortable win - running in seven tries and scoring 34 unanswered points until two late consolation scores for Cook Islands.

Fiji will face reigning champions Australia next, aiming to go one better than their women's team and cause a seismic upset.

"Preparation will be standard," Potter said of getting ready to face Australia. "It is a two-horse race [for the championships] as far as I am concerned, so it is a chance to upset them."

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: Brian McDermott on England's 'erratic' ends and not chasing points with progression out of their hands
articles.summary: England's Rugby League World Cup got off to a poor start with a 30-12 loss to Tonga in Pools B and C; Their progression to the semi-finals is now out of their hands thanks to the unique structure of the Pools; They face France on Saturday October 24 at 7.35am
articles.body:
After an opening round 30-12 loss to Tonga, questions have begun as to whether it worked.

It was clear what England's game plan was from the outset. They were focused on second phase attack and posing a strong attacking threat.

Their forwards fronted up against a powerful Tongan pack but as the game went on, a lack of last play options, structured play in good ball, and errors with ball in hand cost England.

For McDermott, his side managed to pull off the style he was looking for in patches but ultimately, especially at the end of sets, they were "too erratic".

"On occasions, I think we opened up in that first 20 and whether we went through the middle or went through the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position. We had some scrappy finishes to those good ball sets," McDermott said.

"Whether we made an error or even if we got to the end of the set, it was a scrappy finish and it was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga and credit Tonga as well. I thought they were terrific defensively in terms of breaching their line and cracking their line open.

"I thought we did that two or three times in that first half, but they came up with some try-saving tackles. A lot of credit goes to Tonga. The fact that we didn't score on the try-line doesn't suggest that our game plan needs to change. We've just got to be more patient and knock off the ball as much as we can."

Out of England's hands - how can they still get through?

Because of the Rugby League World Cup's unique format, England's chances of getting into the semi-finals are now technically out of their hands following their opening-round loss.

England are in a unique group structure that consists of Groups B and C. Group B is England, Lebanon, Samoa, while Group C is France, Papua New Guinea, Tonga. The structure of Group B and C is that those in one group only play those in the other group.

It means England now have to try and post high scores against France and Papua New Guinea and hope that Tonga beat Samoa convincingly. That way, it would be a straight contest between Samoa and England of who can score the most points.

It goes against McDermott's own ethos to know his side are chasing the tournament and he is cautious of England not becoming so focused on the intricacy of the task at hand that they "trip themselves up".

"We know what's in front of us now. We've got to win the next two games. We've got to improve on the things that we need to improve upon," he added.

"But, again, I've seen enough which is telling me we're heading in the right direction. And, again, when you can identify when you've lost and it's not to do with being physically outdone or strategically outdone, which I don't think it was, it gives me a tremendous amount of confidence.

"It's a bit ironic, isn't it? Because I've just been said about not chasing points and not chasing scoreboards. We certainly don't want to trip ourselves up.

"I don't know. It's going to be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest that we're going to rack a load of points up on Saturday right now. Real early after the game, we'll come up with a plan for France, we'll come up with a plan for PNG."

England must regroup ahead of facing France in Perth next Saturday, kick-off 7.35am (UK and Ireland time).

articles.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews paid emotional tribute in France
articles.summary: Andrews died in France on Friday while on tour with the Johannesburg Lions during the Champions Cup rugby tournament.
articles.body:
Players have stood with their heads bowed, some crying, during a minute’s silence for South African rugby player Hyron Andrews before a Champions Cup game between French side La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions.

Andrews, 31, died in France on Friday on the eve of the game, which was played at the Marcel-Deflandre Stadium in La Rochelle. SA Rugby, the governing body in South Africa, and the Lions confirmed the 31-year-old lock forward’s death.

The number five shirt formerly worn by the player was placed on the field, and his face was shown on the big screen inside the stadium with his full name written out: Hyron Diego Andrews.

Several Lions players were in tears on Saturday while others tilted their heads back and closed their eyes, grabbing each other tightly by the waist.

The crowd at Stade Marcel-Deflandre broke into spontaneous applause after the moment of silence, and a La Rochelle shirt was handed by the French club to the Lions staff.

Television images showed Lions players forming a circle in their dressing room moments before walking out to play the match. La Rochelle players, led out by France forward Gregory Alldritt, wore black armbands.

La Rochelle backs coach Remi Tales told match broadcaster beIN SPORTS that some players from the French side went to offer their support to Lions players at the team hotel on Friday. It was agreed after discussions between the two sides that the game would go ahead, Tales added. La Rochelle won it 31-14.

La Rochelle prosecutor Arnaud Laraize told The Associated Press news agency on Friday that Andrews was found in a shower cubicle, which was locked from the inside, on Friday morning. He had undergone a hammam session about an hour earlier.

Andrews had shown no signs of health problems in the preceding days, according to his entourage. An investigation into the cause of death has been opened and an autopsy was due to be carried out.

SA Rugby said Andrews died after a fall. The player also represented the KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks in England.

“We are heartbroken by the passing of Hyron. He was not only a gifted rugby player but also a cherished member of our Lions family, having recently joined us this season,” said Rudolf Straeuli, the CEO of SA Rugby.

Sale Sharks joined the tributes to Andrews, sending “heartfelt condolences to his wife, their beautiful boys and the rest of his family and friends and everyone at Lions Rugby”.

“Hyron was just a brilliant guy and a brilliant teammate. He was so skilled on the field but, off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with,” Sharks Director of Rugby Alex Sanderson said. “He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him.”

articles.title: Harlequins 57-19 Vannes - Quins run in nine tries to win Challenge Cup opener
articles.summary: Harlequins shrug off poor form in the Prem to score a half-century of points against French side Vannes.
articles.body:
Tries: Murley 2, Smith 2, Hobson, Riley, Evans 2, Staples Cons: Smith 6

Tries: De Benedittis, Benmegal 2 Con: Cotormanac'h 2

Harlequins put aside their difficulties in the early weeks of the new Prem season to start their 2026-27 Challenge Cup campaign with a welcome bonus-point win over French club Vannes.

Quins are bottom of the Prem after losing all three of their matches, but they were far too strong for their visitors, clocking up nine tries.

England back Marcus Smith contributed 22 points courtesy of two tries and six conversions, while there were two tries from captain Cadan Murley and Will Evans and further efforts from Will Hobson, Sam Riley and Jimmy Staples.

Vannes, who are bottom of the Top 14 with four losses out of four, contributed three tries of their own thanks to Wayan De Benedittis and two from winger Enzo Benmegal.

It was Quins' first match at this stage of this competition since 2018 while the Prem outfit have won the Challenge Cup on a record-equalling three occasions, although not since 2011.

But rather than having to front up against a European powerhouse, they had a morale-boosting encounter against a side who won the Pro D2, France's second tier, last season.

Murley and Smith started the scoring before De Benedittis crossed to get the visitors on the board.

Hobson powered over before a deliberate knock-on from Quins fly-half Smith saw him yellow-carded - and with a man less, Benmegal grabbed two tries, including one with a spectacular acrobatic finish.

But in between those, Murley had grabbed his second and with the numbers evened up, the English side dominated the remainder of the contest, as their forwards made hay.

Four of the next five tries came from the pack with Riley, Evans with two and replacement hooker Staples underlining that dominance.

The other try was a second for Smith as he swapped passes with Luke Northmore to claim a double after also grabbing two last Sunday at Sale Sharks in his first appearance of the season.

Harlequins will now look to take the confidence gained from this victory into their Prem derby at home to Saracens next Sunday as they try to get their league campaign up and running.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Pau 41-17 Leicester Tigers - hosts gain bonus point in pool victory
articles.summary: Leicester Tigers begin their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau.
articles.body:
Tries: Marta 2, Zabala, Grandidier Nkanang, Brau-Boirie Cons: Desperes 5 Pens: Desperes 2

Tries: Chessum, Van der Flier Cons: Searle 2 Pen: Searle

Leicester Tigers began their Champions Cup campaign with a 41-17 defeat by French club Pau.

Portugal international Rodrigo Marta crossed for two of the home side's five tries, with a late burst helping them earn a bonus point from their Pool One opener.

Despite falling behind to an early Pau penalty, Leicester did well in the early exchanges, their tactical kicking game keeping them camped in their opponents' territory.

Billy Searle's 50-22 put the Tigers in superb field position and they capitalised through captain Ollie Chessum, who was making his first appearance of the season after recovering from a foot injury.

Pau fought back well, however, showing their quality with three tries in a 20-minute spell either side of half-time.

They had already seen a Sacha Zegueur try ruled out for a knock-on before Marta, the leading try-scorer in this season's Top 14 with six in five appearances, and prop Jon Zebala touched down late in the first half.

Centre Marta raced in again from 30 metres to extend Pau's lead after the interval.

Archie van der Flier powered over in the corner to move Leicester back within seven points, but that would be the final time Leicester would be within range of a losing bonus point, as Pau scored 17 points without reply.

Fly-half Axel Desperes added a further penalty, Theo Attissogbe sent winger Aaron Grandidier Nkanang over unchallenged in the corner and Fabien Brau-Boirie intercepted a Leicester pass to complete the scoring.

Leicester's remaining Pool One matches are against Clermont Auvergne, Glasgow Warriors and Leinster.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Toulouse 43-40 Exeter Chiefs - hosts win classic despite early red card
articles.summary: Toulouse deny Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic contest with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.
articles.body:
Tries: Capuozzo, penalty try, Brennan, Thomas, Remue 2, R Ntamack Cons: R Ntamack 3

Tries: Wimbush 3, Yeandle, Varney, Butt Cons: Slade 5

Toulouse denied Exeter Chiefs a famous Champions Cup victory in France, fighting back to win a frenetic pool game with 14 men following Rodrigue Neti's first-half red card.

Exeter had the chance to force a draw but, with the clock in the red, Henry Slade missed a penalty from about 40 metres out.

Zack Wimbush, starting on the wing for Exeter in place of injured England international Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, scored a hat-trick of tries as the 2020 champions fell just short of winning a classic contest.

Wimbush had put Exeter ahead early, but Toulouse led 12-7 when prop Neti was dismissed in the 16th minute for making shoulder-to-head contact in a tackle on Ross Vintcent.

That incident came during a frantic first half which ended 26-24 in Exeter's favour and included eight tries - four for each side - as well as two yellow cards.

The lead swapped hands several times after the break, but Toulouse grabbed the advantage while Exeter's Ben Hammersley was in the sin-bin to take a narrow victory.

Champions Cup recap: Relive wins for Northampton, Toulouse and Pau

Northampton beat Cardiff for first English win

Late tries give Pau bonus-point win over Leicester

Wimbush's second-minute score stunned the home crowd, but Toulouse replied quickly through Italy's Ange Capuozzo and a penalty try, which also resulted in Exeter full-back Sam Harris being sent to the sin-bin.

Wimbush scored again soon after Neti's early exit, before tries from Joshua Brennan and Teddy Thomas moved Toulouse 10 points in front.

Back came Exeter, now two men to the good after Thomas was yellow-carded for a deliberate knock-on, as Jack Yeandle burrowed over and Stephen Varney touched down under the posts.

After the interval, Will Butt capitalised to extend Exeter's advantage to nine points when Antoine Dupont's clearing kick was charged down, but that was quickly wiped out by some wonderful attacking play by the hosts.

Although Wimbush grabbed his third, Matias Remue's double and another try by Romain Ntamack established a three-point lead for the home team.

There was more drama to follow as Exeter were awarded a late penalty and the visitors went for the posts, but centre Slade pulled his kick just wide, so Exeter had to settle for just a losing bonus point.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Northampton Saints 28-12 Cardiff - Prem club wins Champions Cup opener
articles.summary: Northampton edge to a nervy Champions Cup pool win against tenacious Cardiff at Franklin's Gardens.
articles.body:
Tries: Pater, Thame, Hendy, Dingwall Cons: Belleau 3, Pater

Northampton became the only English side to win in the opening round of the Champions Cup by battling past Cardiff.

Saints, quarter-finalists last season, scored four tries at Franklin's Gardens in a nervy Pool Four encounter.

The English champions led 14-0 at half-time thanks to efforts in tricky conditions by James Pater and Toby Thame.

Tenacious Cardiff struck back through Harri Millard and Mason Grady to make it a two-point game in the final quarter.

But George Hendy and Fraser Dingwall responded as Northampton got off to a winning start, albeit without a bonus point.

Northampton's success came at the end of a chastening opening weekend of the top-tier tournament for Prem clubs, with Gloucester drawing against champions Bordeaux-Begles but six other sides losing.

Champions Cup recap: Relive wins for Northampton, Toulouse and Pau

Toulouse deny Exeter famous Champions Cup victory

Late tries give Pau bonus-point win over Leicester

Cardiff's return to the top tier of Europe after two seasons in the Challenge Cup was a considerable one.

Saints had scored 24 tries in their three opening fixtures of their Prem title defence, including 11 against Bath last time out at Franklin's Gardens.

The Welsh side also had to contend with a five-day turnaround to a United Rugby Championship (URC) fixture against Sharks at Cardiff Arms Park.

That led to several influential players being held back, although they did give first appearances of the season to Wales and Lions internationals Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams after injury.

Northampton also made changes because of a big fixture on the horizon - the short trip to Leicester on Saturday - but got the job done.

Full-back Pater opened the scoring for Saints with a supporting run and centre Thame crashed over after 20 minutes.

Both Northampton number eight Callum Chick and Cardiff lock Tom Manz knocked on going for the line as slippery conditions led to it being 14-0 at half-time.

The Blue and Blacks struck back early in the second half when centre Millard hit a nice line in the 22 and then defended stoutly to frustrate their hosts, forcing them into a raft of handling errors.

It was 14-12 on the hour when, after Saints fly-half Anthony Belleau was sin-binned for a breakdown offence, the ball was floated to the right by Jarrod Evans for Grady to cross.

Cardiff scented an upset only for Hendy to respond swiftly, juggling the ball for a try that Pater converted.

The Northampton wing went from scoring five points to saving them by chasing down Adams when a try seemed certain.

Dingwall dashed over in the 78th minute but the hosts could not find the fifth try that was needed for a five-point haul.

Wales' Thomas to miss Nations Championship restart

Saints travel to Stade Francais in December and return to France in January to face Montpellier before a home finish to the group stage against Bulls.

Cardiff host Bath in December and then face a pair of French teams in January, travelling to Stade Francais and entertaining Montpellier.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Northampton claim first Prem win of tournament as Leicester suffer heavy Pau defeat
articles.summary: Northampton secured a 28-12 win over Cardiff after seven failed attempts from other English sides to win in the Champions Cup this season; Leicester were also well beaten by Pau as they were defeated 41-17; Harlequins won in the Challenge Cup handing Vannes a 57-19 loss
articles.body:
After seven failed attempts from their fellow English sides, the Prem champions were pushed hard by their Welsh visitors, who at one time threatened a comeback at DPD Stadium at Franklin's Gardens.

It took a vital try from man of the match George Hendy to regain control for Saints as they restored some pride on what has been a bruising weekend for teams from their league.

Cardiff made a late change at scrum-half, with South African Johan Mulder coming in for the experienced Aled Davies.

Saints opened the scoring with a superb breakaway try after 12 minutes, with Hendy making the initial charge before passing to Alex Mitchell on the outside.

The England scrum-half's pass back infield reached James Pater and the 19-year-old full-back did well to finish, with Anthony Belleau adding the conversion.

The hosts had some daylight after having a free-kick awarded at a five-metre scrum, with Mitchell quickly finding Rory Hutchinson, whose pass inside sent Toby Thame through.

Saints led 14-0 at half-time, but Cardiff scored a try seven minutes after the restart when Harri Millard crashed in from Mulder's pass, following a tapped penalty, with Jarrod Evans adding the extras.

After Belleau was sin-binned for hands in the ruck near his own line, the visitors moved to within two points when Evans' long pass gave Grady a walk-in for an unconverted try.

Despite being down to 14 men, Northampton extended their lead when Hendy juggled Fraser Dingwall's off-load and just about held on in diving over for a crucial score.

Cardiff were not going quietly and looked certain to haul themselves within reach again when Josh Adams tore away down the left, but Hendy turned from try-scorer to try-saver with a brilliant last-ditch tackle.

Saints finally made sure of victory with a minute to go when the ball was recycled for Dingwall, who glided his way through to cap his fine showing off the bench.

Ollie Chessum made a try-scoring return from injury but Leicester fell short in their opening Champions Cup clash with Pau in the south of France.

Archie van der Flier gave the Tigers a flicker of hope when his 54th-minute try put his side within touching distance but the hosts ultimately pulled away for a 41-17 bonus-point win.

The returning Chessum powered over in his first appearance of the season. But tries from Rodrigo Marta and Jon Zabala gave Pau a half-time lead and when they stretched their advantage through Marta's second early in the second half, it looked all over for the visitors.

Van der Flier had other ideas when he went over, Billy Searle's kick taking them back within seven points, but a careless penalty and subsequent try from Aaron Grandidier Nkanang all but sealed it for the French side.

Pau sealed their bonus point in the dying stages when Searle's attempted pass was intercepted and Fabien Brau-Boirie blazed home to secure an emphatic win.

Marcus Smith shrugged off a first half sin bin to help Harlequins to a 57-19 bonus point win over Vannes in Pool Three of the European Challenge Cup.

England back Smith totalled 22 points from two tries and six conversions, despite enduring a spell on the sidelines for a deliberate knock-on.

It was a much-needed, dominant display from the home side, who managed to shrug off their winless start to the new Gallagher Prem campaign.

Quins were 26-14 up at the interval with Cadan Murley scoring twice and Smith and Will Hobson also crossing the line while the visitors responded through Wayan De Benedittis and winger Enzo Benmegal.

Further tries from Sam Riley and Smith again had Harlequins home and dry by the hour mark.

With the pressure off, Quins stepped up their pursuit of a bonus point, scoring three more tries in the final 15 minutes. Will Evans grabbed his second and third tries of the match, either side of a score from Jimmy Staples.

articles.title: The Wales players that starred before Tandy names Nations Championship squad
articles.summary: Dragons, Ospreys, Scarlets and Cardiff players give Wales boss Steve Tandy plenty to mull over before he names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, 20 October and was given some late food for thought by the Welsh clubs in European action.

Dragons, Ospreys and Scarlets made winning starts in the Challenge Cup while Cardiff competed hard but lost at Northampton on their return to the top-tier Champions Cup.

Wales will face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff before another fixture at Twickenham against a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend.

BBC Sport Wales looks at the players who grasped their last chance to make an impression on Tandy and his staff as opportunities run out before the 2027 World Cup.

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

Cardiff endured a pointless return to the Champions Cup but there were plenty of positives in a battling display at Northampton.

Among them were the returns of experienced Wales internationals Taulupe Faletau and Josh Adams from injury.

Number eight Faletau was impressive when featuring for just shy of an hour on his first outing since March.

He racked up 65 metres with eight carries in the first half and also produced a telling defensive moment to deny opposite number Callum Chick on the try line.

His final act was to carry hard off the base of a scrum, providing more evidence of his ability to come back from injury and swiftly hit high standards.

Tandy picked Faletau for the 2025 autumn internationals only for the number eight to then suffer a knee injury.

The Wales head coach is blessed with a glut of back-row options but will be hoping Faletau, who he worked with on the Lions' tour to South Africa in 2021, stays fit.

Adams came on for the final quarter in the east Midlands and will profit from a first run out, albeit the wing will be stung at having been reeled in by the covering George Hendy when a try seemed certain.

The 31-year-old had a strong 2026 Six Nations and provides Tandy with an experienced and dependable option in the back three.

Cardiff have upcoming United Rugby Championship (URC) games against Sharks at the Arms Park and Ospreys at St Helen's should Wales believe that Faletau and Adams need more minutes before Test consideration.

The Welsh back-row trio starring for Leicester

Wales players in Prem can help Welsh game - Jenkins

Morgan-Williams impresses in problem position

Tomos Williams is a nailed on starter at scrum-half against Japan on Saturday, 7 November but the 21 jersey is up for grabs for the whole month.

There has been talk of trying to tempt Scarlets veteran Gareth Davies out of retirement, with weight added to that argument Kieran Hardy's injury against Dragons.

Ospreys' Reuben Morgan-Williams has been something of a forgotten man amid all that chatter, despite the fact that he came off the bench in Wales' most recent Test match in South Africa.

The 28-year-old made his first start of the season against Black Lion in Tbilisi and produced a lively display in the comfortable win.

Morgan-Williams was to the fore in Ospreys keeping the tempo up and produced an assist Tomos Williams would have been proud of when fizzing a pass past three defenders to the right wing for hooker Lewis Lloyd to go over.

He made two clean breaks, carried the ball 11 times and ran for 77 metres before being taken off with half an hour to go.

The Osprey will be keen to establish Morgan-Williams as deputy to Saracens scrum-half Williams, with Tandy also potentially taking the chance to give livewire Dragons prospect Che Hope a taste of Test camp.

Dragons showed tenacity in defence before securing a hard-fought win against Perpignan in Newport on Friday.

Filo Tiatia's men have made a strong start to the season but that might not necessarily translate into a bigger contingent in Tandy's squad.

Lock Ben Carter is a shoo-in, tight-head prop Dillon Lewis will hope to pick up where he left off in the summer and in-form hooker Elliot Dee would love to battle Dewi Lake and Ryan Elias for action.

The Perpignan fixture highlighted the qualities of Dragons' grafters with blind-side flanker Shane Lewis-Hughes, who won three caps in 2020, continuing his strong start to the season.

Wales contact coach Dan Lydiate was a guest at Dragons training last week and would have been impressed as Lewis-Hughes put in 27 tackles against the French side's big carriers.

But the forward, like team-mate Harri Keddie, is competing in a position of real depth.

The same applies for wing Rio Dyer, who is yet to score this season but has been lively with ball in hand and impressive in the aerial game.

Dragons' man of the match against Perpignan was Aneurin Owen, so often the side's glue from inside centre.

He carried strongly to go with his distribution skills, while he was strong in defence and came up with two turnovers.

Owen, who turns 26 the day before Tuesday's squad announcement, was a member of the Wales squad under Wayne Pivac in the summer of 2021 but remains uncapped.

There might be an opening at 12 due to Ben Thomas' injury should Tandy look to see if a quality operator at club level can take the next step.

"Aneurin knows I love him," said Dragons boss Filo Tiatia. "He has outstanding leadership and there is lots more to come from him.

"He wants to improve, is coachable and is strong at challenging the coaches."

WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman

End use of artificial pitches - Rees-Zammit

Wales fly-half Sam Costelow provided a scare by coming off with a hamstring injury at the end of the first half in Scarlets' thumping of Newcastle Red Bulls , with director of rugby Nigel Davies describing it as a precaution.

Ellis Mee demonstrated why he is a definite selection with a player-of-the-match performance and his fellow wing Macs Page marked his 50th appearance for the club with two tries.

"He a good rugby player, he's got a good brain," said Davies of the 21-year-old.

"He can read the picture in front of him and that's his role, to roam and try and create carnage when he's on the ball.

"He came onto the scene with a bang but probably things didn't go his way in the second season. Now we're starting to see the potential he's got."

Wales might have wanted to see more of back-rower Taine Plumtree in his first game back after shoulder surgery but captain Josh Macleod demonstrated his ability again with a series of turnovers.

The flanker has fallen down the Wales pecking order but has been Scarlets' leading forward so far this season.

"Josh had a fantastic game," said Davies. "There were probably four or five turnovers by him and they were big moments in the game."

Scarlets players selected by Wales are unlikely to travel to South Africa on Tuesday for URC matches with Stormers and Bulls because the international squad meet up next Monday.

articles.title: 'Security incident' at Northampton during Cardiff game believed to be a hoax
articles.summary: Police are investigating the incident at Saints' Franklin's Gardens "following threats made on social media".
articles.body:
A 'security incident' during Northampton's Champions Cup win over Cardiff on Sunday is believed to have been a hoax.

Police were called to the Saints' Franklin's Gardens stadium at about 19:00 BST "following threats made on social media".

The game had kicked off at 17:30 and players from both sides left the field straight after the final whistle as a "precautionary measure".

"Enquiries into the incident remain ongoing and we are working closely with both the Saints and our policing partners on the investigation," said a Northamptonshire Police spokeswoman.

Northampton, who won the Champions Cup match 28-12, said they were "sorry that supporters didn't get the opportunity to see the players after the final whistle".

They added: "Following a security incident at the stadium, both sides left the field immediately as a precautionary measure.

"Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

"The safety of our supporters, players, staff and officials will always remain our top priority."

articles.title: Ieuan Evans: Former Wales captain leaving role as Lions chair
articles.summary: British and Irish Lions are looking for a new chair as former Wales captain Ieuan Evans' term comes to an end after almost four years.
articles.body:
Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role.

The former Wales captain, who played on tours to Australia in 1989, New Zealand in 1993 and South Africa in 1997, was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term.

Ex-wing Evans was tour manager last year when the men's team recorded a series victory against the Wallabies under Andy Farrell.

The Lions have started the search for a new chair before next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand.

"I am incredibly proud of what has been achieved over the past four years, particularly the success of the 2025 tour, the progress made towards the first Lions Women's tour and the strength of the organisation as it looks ahead to an exciting new chapter," said Evans.

Northampton 'security incident' believed to be a hoax

The players that staked late claims for Wales spots

The 62-year-old, who scored the Lions' pivotal series-winning try in the third Test against Australia in 1989, oversaw governance changes with the recruitment of independent directors to the board.

Lions chief executive Ben Calveley said: "His infectious passion for the Lions and understanding of what makes this organisation so special has been evident throughout his time in the role."

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: What we learnt from England's opener, the Australia Test, and ignoring points required
articles.summary: England women showed their style in a massive opening 70-4 win over Wales; England men suffered a 30-12 defeat to Tonga and their Rugby League World Cup is now out of their hands; Izzy Rowe shined for England, with the men's half-backs leaving questions
articles.body:
​​​​Both England teams are considered underdogs to make it through to the semi-finals, with the task now getting even greater for the men's side after that loss to what looks to be potentially the strongest Tonga team we have ever seen.

Meanwhile, England women prep for Australia - a feat that will be their biggest to date.

So, what did we learn from their openers and what can we expect moving forward into week two? Let's take a look...

Second phase play brings errors but opportunity

England men had a clear tactic in their match against Tonga - second phase play. They were offloading the ball freely and constantly trying to create opportunity and space. In all fairness, it worked and got them into try-scoring positions on the field.

In the first half in particular, they looked a real attacking threat. That is, until they got within the opposition's 20 metres.

It was then, that their last play options and attacking options, let them down. They had 27 offloads compared to Tonga's five. They had 246 passes compared to Tonga's 191. Despite that, they made over 70 more tackles than Tonga and not only that, they put up just five bombs - Tonga had 12.

They did not pressurise and become clinical in the moments that mattered and it meant that, when momentum went the other way, they had no points on the board to show for their pressure.

At 10-6 down, they conceded one of the luckiest tries from a kick you might see - a ricochet of the flukiest variety.

Brian McDermott admitted that his style of play was risky. He said that they would try things and sometimes they would come off and sometimes they would not. In the first half, England had made nine errors while Tonga had made just three.

There seemed to be a spark to England, a flair somewhat for 80 metres of the pitch but in the final 20, ideas faded away.

Strongest Tonga, travel day(s), and missing grunt

Of course, it is important to put the loss to Tonga into context. Many England fans will be ruing that this match was not the closing match of the Pool stages for England rather than their opener.

After just about a week together, with no mid-season internationals, England travelled across the world from Heathrow, to Sydney, then Perth, and did what they could in seven days. To call them far from ideal circumstances is to put it lightly.

Not only that, their forward pack was not what they would have wanted. Morgan Smithies was ruled out of the tournament, another enforcer in Morgan Knowles was then ruled out of the game. Add to that the fact Matty Lees, Caleb Hamlin-Uele, and Mike McMeeken were not options and the grunt we expect from a traditional England outfit wanes.

England were also coming up against what is arguably the strongest Tonga team we have ever seen. Kristian Woolf has some real star talent to pick from.

Robert Toia is up there as one of the best centres in the world alongside Herbie Farnworth. Toluta'u Koula, in the other centre spot, played State of Origin this year as did Addin Fonua-Blake and Stefano Utoikamanu.

Toia, Siua Wong, and Salesi Foketi won the Grand Final with the Sydney Roosters in 2026. Haumole Olakau'atu was voted the second rower of the year. Youngster Isaiya Katoa is considered a superstar in the making in the halves.

When written down on paper, they were always an exceptional feat to take on.

England women shone in their opener against Wales women and one player who justified her selection and then some was player of the match Izzy Rowe.

The big talking point before the match was who would be chosen out of Rowe, woman of Steel Jenna Foubister, and NRLW star Georgia Roche in the halves. England head coach Stu Barrow opted for Rowe and Roche, starting Foubister on the bench.

Rowe went onto show just why as she scored the most points ever by an England player in a match. She excelled with the ball in hand but her kicking game was also exceptional both in play and off the tee. It is an attribute that makes her somewhat of a necessity in the side and she showed why.

Foubister came on and showed her worth too, pulling off a brilliant assist, but it is a welcome problem for England moving forward.

Talking of moving forward, England women will have to box off a strong opening result and focus on the enormous task they have up next - facing the reigning and defending champions Australia.

Last time these two sides met, it was a sobering outing for England back in 2025 as they fell to a 90-4 loss to the Jillaroos in Las Vegas. It was a stark reminder of the gulf between the two teams and the journey English rugby league still has to go.

However, only a handful of players from that match remain in this international side and it is the chance for a lot of sensational youngsters to show that England have improved. Ensuring it stays as close a game as possible will be vital for England.

Last out, they will face Samoa who were beaten 40-0 by Australia. Points difference could be the key distinguisher of who makes it through to the semi-finals.

Underdogs mentality to shine through again

The underdog mentality for the England teams is going to have to shine through in week two but in different ways.

England women know they have their toughest task ahead but they are buoyant and will be fired up to show just what talent they have in their ranks.

England men, meanwhile, know they are up against it. They are in a complicated combined Group B and Group C.

Group B is England, Lebanon, Samoa, while Group C is France, Papua New Guinea, Tonga. After losing to Tonga, England now have France and PNG to play because you play the teams in the other group, not your own.

It means that, if results go as expected, England are effectively hoping for Tonga to beat Samoa and then be a straight shoot out with the Samoans for who can come away with the better results.

Remarkably, in the Rugby League World Cup 2022, Samoa got demolished by England in their opening game but then went on to beat them in the semi-final. England are afforded no such breathing room.

England must regroup ahead of facing France in Perth next Saturday, kick-off 7.35am (UK and Ireland time). Meanwhile, England women face Australia at 10.05am.

articles.title: Glasgow Warriors: Jamie Ritchie to make debut against Benetton
articles.summary: Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut this weekend.
articles.body:
Glasgow assistant coach Nigel Carolan says the time has finally come to "unleash" former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie for his Warriors debut.

The former Edinburgh flanker signed from French club Perpignan in the summer but has been sidelined for the opening months of the season because of ankle and Achilles tendon issues.

The 30-year-old, capped 63 times, is now back in full training and is expected to play in Saturday's United Rugby Championship (URC) match against Benetton in Treviso.

"He's training fully. We feel he's integrated into the systems now very well. And he's itching to go," said Carolan.

"It would be great if we get him involved this week, either starting or on the bench. It would be really positive to have him involved, especially ahead of Scotland's Nations Cup in a couple of weeks."

Ritchie was a pillar of the Edinburgh team for more than a decade before moving to the French Top 14 side.

Carolan believes patience will pay off for the Warriors with Ritchie, who has moved to Scotstoun on a two-year deal.

"I think it was important to get the timing right. We didn't want to rush him," the Irishman added.

"Obviously he had surgery over the summer so we didn't really want to push him. He's just moved to a new club and with all that going on, we felt the timing needed to be right.

"We could have involved him maybe last week but that was Ruwald van der Merwe's time. So I think the time has now come to unleash Jamie Ritchie in a Glasgow Warriors shirt."

Warriors are second in the URC table after three matches - behind Edinburgh - and will be favourite against second-bottom Benetton this weekend.

They finished top of the URC last season but were knocked out of the play-offs in the semi-finals by the Bulls and the arrivals of Ritchie and Van der Merwe - with Scotland back row Jack Dempsey departing - were part of an evolution of Franco Smith's squad in the summer.

articles.title: Tomos Williams: Do Wales need a Plan B before 2027 World Cup?
articles.summary: Wales boast a world-class scrum-half in Tomos Williams but Steve Tandy might have to assess his back-up before the 2027 World Cup.
articles.body:
There are few, if any, players more secure of a starting spot at next year's World Cup in Australia than Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams.

France superstar Antoine Dupont has a rival for the nine jersey in Maxime Lucu, a talisman for back-to-back European champions Bordeaux-Begles.

Malcolm Marx, World Rugby player of the year, fights hard for his start as South Africa's hooker but must also be prepared for 'bomb squad' duty from the bench.

The best players on the planet usually have a rival pushing them hard, but there is a gulf between 2025 British and Irish Lions tourist Williams and his fellow Welsh nines.

Wales have 12 or 13 fixtures to play before their 2027 World Cup opener against Zimbabwe in Adelaide on 2 October.

Steve Tandy needs wins to build momentum but does the head coach, who names his Nations Championship squad on Tuesday, also need to work on a contingency plan at scrum-half?

The players that staked late claims for Wales spots

Wales counting down the year until World Cup

Williams has started every Test he has been available for since Tandy took the reins in the summer of 2025.

The only fixtures he has missed - last November's defeat by South Africa and June's win in the uncapped game against the Barbarians - were outside World Rugby's international window.

The former Cardiff scrum-half, who swapped Gloucester for Saracens in the summer, has played past the hour in every outing under Tandy.

Wales won three Tests in 2025-26 and Williams played the full 80 minutes against Japan and Fiji, while he came off with just two minutes left against Italy.

The 31-year-old played 378 minutes in the 2026 Six Nations, with 10 of those minutes on the sidelines due to a yellow card against Ireland.

In comparison, France's Dupont played 357 (Lucu was injured), Ireland's Jamison Gibson-Park 323 and Scotland's Ben White 302.

Williams has shared matchday squads with just two scrum-halves under Tandy - Ospreys' Kieran Hardy and Reuben Morgan-Williams.

Hardy, who started against South Africa and the Baa-Baas, made five brief appearances off the bench while Morgan-Williams came on three times.

But there is likely to be a new inclusion when Tandy names his group for the Nations Championship.

Hardy faces a lengthy lay-off after suffering a knee injury against Dragons earlier this month.

His misfortune could lead to more opportunities for Morgan-Williams, who has had to show patience at international level.

Ospreys head coach Mark Jones said of him last season: "He's a real competitor and has got a real appetite on both sides of the ball. He injects speed into the game.

"What I like about him is his personality. He's just straight-talking, no messing around."

Tandy must find a third specialist as he counts down to the World Cup, where he will have another decision to make.

Warren Gatland initially went with two scrum-halves in 2023 - Williams and Gareth Davies - before adding Hardy for injured number eight Taulupe Faletau before the quarter-final defeat by Argentina.

Dragons scrum-half Che Hope was touted as a possible summer tourist with Wales until he suffered a hamstring injury last February.

The 23-year-old has returned this season to share starts with Rhodri Williams, who won the last of his nine caps in the 2025 Six Nations.

Wales might opt to take a look at the lively Hope but Dragons defence coach Dale MacLeod has urged caution with a player who has made just 30 senior appearances.

"Che is quick, exciting and can turn nothing into something," said the New Zealander.

"He is a great support runner and is starting to become a much better defensive player.

"He is growing his game nicely and with all younger boys coming through you need to have a blend by giving opportunities without throwing them in the deep end.

"Che will only grown and get better because he is still a young man and I am looking forward to him getting some unhindered time in the saddle."

Davies urged to reverse retirement for World Cup

If Williams is the nailed-on starter then Tandy might have another option to either add impact or finish the job from the bench.

Gareth Davies retired from Test rugby in 2024, having won 77 Wales caps, a Grand Slam and a Six Nations title.

He went on two British and Irish Lions tours and featured in the 2015, 2019 and 2023 World Cups.

Davies is still going strong for Scarlets and, although he started against Newcastle last Saturday, the veteran has got used to a new role as a replacement.

"He struggled with it for the first couple of years because he is such a competitor and wants to start," admitted Scarlets director of rugby Nigel Davies.

"He is mellowing into that role where he can come on and make an impact."

The scrum-half will be 37 when the World Cup takes place but his former team-mate Jonathan Davies believes age is not a problem.

"He has always been one of the most fiercely competitive animals in the rugby environment," said the former Scarlets, Wales and Lions centre on Scrum V podcast.

"He looks after himself and is a great pro. He can definitely still do it."

Davies has been suggested as an emergency option for Wales , but Scarlets coach Dwayne Peel is quick to point out the qualities of Dane Blacker, who has started all three United Rugby Championship (URC) games so far.

"He's a player who wants to play the game quickly and he's been very, very good for us," said former Wales scrum-half Peel.

"I'm really happy with the way he's gone about his business. He's one who could definitely push if you want to play that quick, expansive game."

Ten Welsh scrum-halves have played for regions so far this season - Blacker, Gareth Davies and Archie Hughes at Scarlets, Hardy, Morgan-Williams and Luke Davies at Ospreys, Hope and Rhodri Williams at Dragons, Ellis Bevan, Aled Davies and Sion Davies at Cardiff.

Wales are blessed with a world-class scrum-half in Tomos Williams, but Tandy might have to prepare a plan B.

articles.title: Canada v England: How have Canada closed gap to Red Roses?
articles.summary: Forty-one matches, four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but England's unbeaten run is over. So how did Canada close the gap to the Red Roses?
articles.body:
Forty-one matches, nearly four years and one Rugby World Cup triumph - but the Red Roses' unbeaten streak is over.

It fell to the experienced Amy Cokayne to face the press this week after England lost their first match since 2022 against Canada.

"You can't dwell on it," said the Sale hooker, who has 95 international caps.

"We weren't a million miles away, so it's not like we have to completely throw the book out - nothing needs to massively change to the way we play."

As with every team in the women's game, the Red Roses have dominated Canada over recent years.

Before this autumn, the two teams had met seven times this decade. England had won every match, with an average victory margin of nearly 22 points.

But that rivalry is nowhere near as comfortable for the Red Roses now.

After a 26-26 draw at Exeter's Sandy Park in September, Canada ended England's long unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto on Friday.

So how have Canada managed to close the gap on the world champions?

And how will the Red Roses react to their first loss under head coach John Mitchell?

When England and Canada met in last year's World Cup final, the hosts ultimately ran out comfortable winners in Twickenham.

But Canada were disappointed with their performance in defeat - and rightly so.

Canada's dismantling of New Zealand in the semi-finals - a performance bubbling with rapid-fire ruck speed and intricate, accurate handling - was the best display of any team in the tournament.

Canada have not been as consistent as England. They have suffered defeats by New Zealand and France this year. But at their best they are capable of a higher standard than any of the Red Roses' rivals.

With a record-breaking home crowd of 18,621 roaring them on in Toronto, in a match marketed as a chance for World Cup revenge, Canada came to the boil perfectly.

Beyond the emotional, there are also structural elements that Canada have right.

Head coach Kevin Rouet, along with plenty of his players, have been gaining experience in England's PWR.

While Canada lacks a professional women's domestic league, England's is the strongest in the world, giving Rouet's players a level of training and match experience they cannot find anywhere else.

Canada have brought in some exciting new talents since the last Rugby World Cup who will be interesting teams on this side of the Atlantic.

Number eight Lizzie Gibson made her Test debut in April and has been a hard-carrying option at the base of the scrum.

England have also been forced to blood new options.

With regular captain Zoe Stratford, second rows Abbie Ward and Rosie Galligan, and back row Marlie Packer all absent, and wing Abby Dow retired, they have not got the same depth or experience of a year ago.

What is harder to discern than the on-pitch inaccuracies is the Red Roses' psychological state.

For so long, they have been out on their own at the top of the women's game.

For many of their fixtures over the past four years, they have set internal statistical goals to strive for, because victory was all but a given.

To find the motivation to push on uphill after summiting the mountain of a home World Cup is hard.

The squad rallied round to produce a backs-to-the-wall defence of their Six Nations title in the immediate aftermath, but perhaps this defeat is both a symptom of, and a cure for, a lack of obvious goals to chase.

The rematch of the rematch - on Friday in Ottawa - is surely the perfect fuel to fire up England.

articles.title: England rugby league: Brian McDermott names unchanged team for World Cup match against France
articles.summary: England's Brad O'Neill has dismissed the suggestion they were underprepared for their Rugby League World Cup campaign as they bid to start salvaging it with an unchanged team against France.
articles.body:
Brad O'Neill has dismissed the suggestion that England were underprepared for their Rugby League World Cup campaign as they bid to start salvaging it with an unchanged team against France this Saturday.

England are under pressure - and in huge danger of missing out on a semi-final spot - after losing last Saturday's opening match 30-12 to Tonga, but head coach Brian McDermott has kept faith with the same 19-man squad.

McDermott's side have had a tight turnaround for the tournament - the Tonga match was just 14 days after the 2026 Super League Grand Final, with England flying out to Australia 10 days before the game.

They did not play a warm-up match - and so went into the game having not played a single international fixture since losing to Australia in Headingley in November last year.

Defeat by Tonga came in McDermott's first match in charge since being appointed in April, and O'Neill said they are "new team" and "those little things should come together".

But when asked by BBC Sport if England were tired and underprepared for Tonga, the 2026 Super League Man of Steel said: "Not at all, we had a great week of prep heading into the tournament.

"The whole team felt really good physically, it was just a good game and the better team won."

McDermott had said he would "have a look" at team selection after Tonga, but has decided to stick with same XIII for this Saturday's match.

He also said England "were not strategically outdone" despite the heavy loss and only needed tweaks rather than a tactical overhaul.

"Only having a week together, those little things should come together and we should start executing with practice," said O'Neill.

"We're not changing anything we play, it is about the execution side of things. It is those combinations in training and bringing those to the match.

"There is a real belief in the team, we are a new team. We need time to work on combos, hopefully those will pay off."

AJ Brimson retains his place at full-back in the XIII with Jack Welsby among the interchanges for Saturday's Group B-C match in Perth (kick-off 07:35 BST).

Luke Thompson will continue at prop with Morgan Knowles still not fit to play after picking up an injury before the Tonga game.

And Mikey Lewis, who was a much-debated pick for the squad as one of the half-backs ahead of 2025 Super League Man Of Steel Jake Connor, remains out of the team.

Harry Smith will continue alongside England captain George Williams in the half-back roles, despite both being overpowered by Tonga last weekend.

That defeat, England's first ever against Tonga, has left McDermott's side with a tough task to reach the semi-finals.

Group B-C works as a combined pool of six teams, from which only the top two will reach the semi-finals. England, in Group B, are facing the three teams in Group C - Tonga, France and Papua New Guinea.

Qualification gets complicated if teams are level on points: Head-to-head record is the first tiebreaker - which would go against England if they finished level with Tonga. But points difference will be used if two teams in the group have not played each other - which would be the case if England and Samoa needed to be separated.

England must win their next two games, against France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October, to stand a realistic chance of progression - and because of the World Cup's format, probably need to win them both by a big score.

Even then, there is the strong possibility that England will not know their fate for certain until two days after their final match, when Tonga face 2022 finalists Samoa in their last group game.

"We have discussed what is required, but we are taking it day by day," said O'Neill. "We are confident we can do it.

"We just focus on a game at the time and don't think much about format.

"Mentally we can't go in thinking about points, if we do our job well enough we will get the win."

Foubister, 19, to start against Australia

In contrast to McDermott, England women's coach Stuart Barrow has made a big selection change before their blockbuster meeting with co-hosts Australia on Saturday.

Jenna Foubister will start at half-back, replacing Georgia Roche, after a superb year in the Super League where she was named Woman of Steel.

The 19-year-old, who scored on her debut in a 62-0 win against Wales in August 2025, will partner Izzy Rowe in the halves.

Rowe scored two tries and kicked nine conversions for 26 points as England opened their World Cup campaign with a 70-6 win against Wales last Saturday.

She equalled the record for the most points by an individual England player in a Women's World Cup match.

There are two other changes to the XIII, as Molly Jones replaces Georgia Wilson in the centres while Liv Wood plays at prop ahead of Mary Coleman.

Lucie Sams is named among the interchanges as England take on reigning champions Australia in Perth with kick-off at 10.05 BST - immediately after the men's match.

It will be the first time England have played Australia since they suffered their record defeat - 90-4 - in Las Vegas in March 2025.

"It's definitely a challenge - we would be naive to go into it not thinking it would be really tough," said England wing Anna Davies.

"But we approach it having grown from the last time we faced them, it is exciting to see the changes we have made. I think we can control a game much better than last time.

"I love getting the chance to play them. It's a chance to have a go at the best in the world."

Wales - playing at their first Women's Rugby League World Cup - have made a number of changes for Friday's match against Samoa (07:45 BST).

Amberley Ruck replaces Ffion Lewis, with Zoe Heeley moving from centre to the wing.

Jade Mullen comes into the centres, while wing Sian Williams also gets a start.

Australia coach Kevin Walters has dropped Reece Walsh to the bench for their second group game against Fiji on Sunday (09:05 GMT), with James Tedesco coming in at full-back.

Tedesco will also captain the co-hosts, as Isaah Yeo - who has delayed surgery on a torn pectoral muscle to play at the World Cup - is rested.

Walsh, who had not played since 15 August amid injury troubles, started as Australia were pushed by New Zealand in a thrilling World Cup opening match last Thursday.

He scored a try but kicked just two of five conversions as the Aussies squeezed to a 24-22 win at Sydney Football Stadium.

Tedesco steps up as one of five changes made by Walters. Bradman Best, Sam Walker and Blayke Brailey all come in for their Test debuts.

articles.title: Wales name uncapped Dragons Aneurin Owen and Che Hope in Nations Championship squad
articles.summary: Wales include uncapped Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Che Hope in the squad for November Nations Championship Tests but Taulupe Faletau misses out.
articles.body:
Uncapped Dragons centre Aneurin Owen and scrum-half Che Hope have been included in Wales' squad for the Nations Championship.

Steve Tandy has selected a 39-strong group for the November Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake named as captain.

The head coach calls up Dragons lock Seb Davies and Cardiff number eight Taine Basham for the first time since he took charge of the national side.

Cardiff loose-head prop Rhys Barratt, who played in the summer fixture against the Barbarians, is the third uncapped player in the squad, while Dragons wing Rio Dyer earns a recall.

Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell and fit-again number eight Taulupe Faletau are among the notable absentees.

Wales face Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff and finish against a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend at Twickenham.

Will Wales tackle reliance on Williams before World Cup?

Ref Whitehouse retires to join Wales coaching team

Owen was a member of the Wales squad in the summer of 2021 but did not feature in the Tests against Canada or Argentina.

The 26-year-old from Newport has been a key member of the Dragons side that has built on an encouraging 2025-26 with a promising start to the season.

Owen gets his chance in the absence of injured Cardiff centre Ben Thomas to join Eddie James, Joe Hawkins, Max Llewellyn and Louie Hennessey as a midfield option.

Hope, 23, is brought in for a first taste of international camp and joins Tomos Williams and Reuben Morgan-Williams, with Kieran Hardy facing a lengthy lay-off after a knee injury.

There is no place for in-form Scarlets wing Macs Page, but Dragons' Dyer, who has also started the season strongly, does earn a recall.

The 26-year-old won the most recent of his 24 caps against South Africa last November.

Leicester's Gabriel Hamer-Webb, who made his Wales debut against Scotland in the Six Nations, also returns after missing out in the summer.

Lock Davies, who moved from Cardiff to Dragons in the summer of 2025, will aim to win his first cap since the 2022 Six Nations.

Dynamic back-row forward Basham has started the season strongly for Cardiff and gets the nod ahead of fit-again Faletau, who made his first appearance of the season for Cardiff at Northampton on Sunday.

Wales' back-row riches mean that there is no place in the squad for specialist open-side Reffell, who featured in the summer Tests and has been in fine form for Leicester.

Lock Dafydd Jenkins, tight-heads Tomas Francis and Archie Griffin, hooker Liam Belcher and centre Hennessey return after being unavailable for the July Tests against Fiji, Argentina and South Africa.

Belcher gets the nod ahead of Elliot Dee, the leading try scorer in the United Rugby Championship (URC), as the third hooker behind captain Lake and Ryan Elias.

Tandy said: "It's great to welcome back the players who were unavailable for the first three rounds of the Nations Championship.

"Added to that, there are a number of players who've been in great form for their clubs and so we wanted to give them an opportunity in the squad this autumn."

The squad features 14 players from clubs in England plus Montpellier lock Adam Beard.

There are seven call-ups for Cardiff and Scarlets, six for Dragons and four from Ospreys.

There is a round of URC action this weekend and back-row forward Taine Plumtree and centre Hawkins have been allowed to travel to South Africa with Scarlets for their fixture against Stormers on Saturday.

articles.title: Taulupe Faletau: Wales great backed to push for 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: Wales boss Steve Tandy believes Taulupe Faletau is a World Cup contender despite missing out on the Nations Championship squad.
articles.body:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy believes legendary number eight Taulupe Faletau is still fueled by playing at a fourth World Cup.

The 35-year-old was left out of Wales' squad for the Nations Championship, having only made his return from injury in Cardiff's Champions Cup defeat by Northampton on Sunday.

Faletau showed his class during a 55-minute appearance against the English champions but will remain with Cardiff rather than hunting a first cap since facing Japan in the summer of 2025.

"It's great to see him back, and you see how quickly he picks up the game from not having a lot of rugby," said Tandy.

"He is a legend of our game and a world-class player, so we would definitely not rule anyone out."

Faletau has won 109 Wales caps but has not played under Tandy, who opted to select in-form Taine Basham to rival Aaron Wainwright in November's squad.

The head coach also used Olly Cracknell and Taine Plumtree at number eight in his first year in charge.

Tandy picked Faletau in his first squad, but the former Dragons back-rower then suffered a knee injury for Cardiff, before a Six Nations call-up was also shelved due to a calf issue.

"I haven't spoken to Toby since Cardiff's game, but I've had chats with him over the period that I have been in charge, because he was going to be in the first two campaigns," said Tandy, a former flanker.

"I've spoken to Toby about being fit and available; then we can cross that bridge when he has put some consistent rugby together."

Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call

Ref Whitehouse retires to join Wales coaching team

Cardiff Rugby appoint Barnsley's Flatman as CEO

Faletau played at the 2011, 2015 and 2023 World Cups but missed the 2019 edition after breaking his collarbone during the build-up.

Tandy believes that the number eight, who played Tests on three Lions tours, will want to be in the mix for next year's tournament in Australia.

"Toby is competitive. He loves playing for Cardiff and loves playing for Wales, so I can see the drive in him," he said.

"If he's out on the field, then he's not playing just to play for Cardiff; I think Toby has ambition to play for Wales."

Faletau, whose father Kuli played for Tonga at the 1999 World Cup, has the motivation but needs to show that he has the durability.

He racked up games for club and country when at Dragons but has played only 31 times for Cardiff since joining from Bath in 2022.

"With the older athlete, you're not going to ask them to play 80 minutes every week," said Tandy.

"You need to have enough evidence that they are going to be robust enough for a World Cup campaign, when you only take a squad of 33.

"You have to be robust to play back-to-back games, which I'm hopeful Toby can do.

"You have to manage players. Even the boys that are at their prime physically probably can't back up 80 minutes every week either."

Faletau will aim to show he is ready if needed for the November Tests in Cardiff against Japan, New Zealand, Australia and another opponent on Nations Championship finals weekend.

Cardiff host Sharks at the Arms Park on Friday in the United Rugby Championship (URC) before finishing the first block of the season at Ospreys.

articles.title: Dominic Silvester: Saracens owner backs CEO amid 'executive-level chaos' claims
articles.summary: Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has full confidence in CEO Ed Coetzee, rejecting claims of "executive-level chaos".
articles.body:
Saracens owner Dominic Silvester says he has "full confidence" in chief executive Ed Coetzee and dismissed a newspaper article suggesting there was "executive-level chaos" at the club.

In an open letter on Saracens' website , external , responding to an article in The Times last week, Silvester said Coetzee had achieved an "extraordinary amount" since being appointed in July.

"The board has full confidence in Ed and his team," Silvester wrote.

"We believe they have the experience, capability and determination to raise standards across every area of the club, strengthen our financial sustainability and ensure that Saracens continues to be an organisation of which our players, staff, partners and supporters can be proud."

The Times article, published on Friday , external , claimed the 2022 takeover in which Silvester assumed control from former owner Nigel Wray had "triggered a period of executive-level chaos", pointing to Coetzee being Sarries' third chief executive in two years and alleging a high turnover of staff.

"With such a churn in executive staff, club sponsors may well be reluctant to engage in relationship-building," the article added.

But Silvester used his open letter to reject the suggestions and listed Coetzee's achievements, such as bringing the all-female athletics meeting Athlos and the Gaelic football fixture between Mayo and Kerry to the club's StoneX Stadium.

He also highlighted the securing of new commercial and hospitality partnerships and a beefed-up executive team, with Jason Thomas as chief financial officer and Rob Cook as chief operating officer.

"Together, Ed, Jason and Rob bring significant experience, complementary expertise and a clear commitment to building a financially sustainable business while maintaining Saracens' high-performance sporting ambitions," Silvester wrote.

"We are ambitious about our future, realistic about the work required to achieve our goals and united in our commitment to taking Saracens forward."
